facts.about: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.

flags.text: Profit compounding (+8%/yr) lags sales (+17%/yr) over 3 years — margins under pressure
Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 105% of PAT

business.summary: Avenue Supermarts Limited operates DMart, a national supermarket chain focusing on value-retailing through an everyday low cost/everyday low price model, offering foods, non-foods, general merchandise, and apparel products to middle-class consumers.

segments.name: Food and Grocery
segments.note: Accounts for about 32% of total organised retail industry in value terms.

guidance.statement: Internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base annually.
guidance.quote: So I do want to state that internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually.

guidance.statement: Open at least 10% to 20% of base stores every year.
guidance.quote: Like we have always said that the right method of expansion in the offline space is to open on an average every year at least 10% to 15% or maybe 10% to 20% of your base stores – every year.

guidance.statement: DMart Ready business can be broken even in a couple of years.
guidance.quote: So, I can't give any forward-looking points of view on when will it be profitable or breakeven or all that. But broadly, we feel that this is a business that can be broken even in a couple of years.

guidance.statement: Blended gross margin will remain in the range of 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%.
guidance.quote: I think 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%, those are the kind of ranges we play in from a gross margin standpoint.

guidance.statement: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores.
guidance.quote: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores.

guidance.statement: You can take a range of 40 to 60 stores over the next three years.
guidance.quote: So, you can take a range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.

scorecard.promised: Open 40-50 stores in FY25 and 40-60 stores annually over the next three years.
scorecard.delivered: Opening pace remains at approximately 40 stores annually based on historical trends.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue grew 16.9% in Mar 2025, but management is still being pushed on why additions are capped at 40.

scorecard.promised: Internally benchmarked to open around 10% to 20% of the store base annually.
scorecard.delivered: Current pace is below the 15% target as store count hit 500 recently.
scorecard.evidence: With a 500-store base, 15% growth requires 75 new stores; current run rate is closer to 40-50.

scorecard.promised: Blended gross margin to remain in the range of 14.5% to 15.5%.
scorecard.delivered: Operating margins have stabilized at 7% to 8% through Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Operating margins were 8% in Jun 2026 and 7% in Sep 2026, consistent with long-term 8% annual averages.

scorecard.promised: The e-commerce business can be broken even in a couple of years.
scorecard.delivered: Subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce Limited continues to report losses.
scorecard.evidence: Annual report notes continued losses with an investment carrying value of ₹1,488.11 crore.

narrative.scoreline: Management maintains steady operational margins and revenue growth, but struggles to accelerate physical store expansion to meet their ambitious 15% annual growth benchmarks.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Quick commerce is not significantly impacting metro revenues.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue growth slowed from 18.9% in Mar 2026 to 14.9% in Jun 2026.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: General merchandise and apparel gross margin contribution will stay around 23%.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins remained flat at 8% for FY2025 and FY2026 despite this mix.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Full year turnover for FY24 was close to 67,000 crores with 7.8% EBITDA.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Actual Mar 2024 revenue was ₹50,789 cr; the ₹68,821 cr figure was reached in Mar 2026.

bull: Revenue compounding remains strong, growing from ₹50,789 cr in 2024 to ₹68,821 cr by March 2026.
Excellent cash generation with 5-year operating cash flow representing 105% of reported PAT.
Strong balance sheet maintained with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x despite aggressive expansion.
bear: Profit compounding at 8% significantly lags sales growth of 17%, indicating persistent margin pressure.
Free Cash Flow remains negative at -₹646 cr in Mar 2026 due to heavy capital expenditure.
E-commerce subsidiary continues to accumulate losses, requiring a ₹1,488 cr investment carrying value.
watch: Check if FY27 store additions exceed the historical 40-50 store ceiling.

claims.claim: We entered five new states last year and hit the 500-store milestone.
claims.quote: So last year, we entered five new states, and we also hit the 500-store milestone.

claims.claim: We double down on DMart Ready in 11 key cities to prove a sustainable, profitable e-commerce model.
claims.quote: We made a conscious choice to double down on DMart Ready in 11 key cities where the vast majority of our online business comes from.

claims.claim: Full year turnover close to 67000 crores, EBITDA margin at 7.8%, and PAT at 4.8%.
claims.quote: We reported a turnover of close to INR67,000 crores in the year gone by. EBITDA margin came in at about 7.8%. Profit after tax was about 4.8%

claims.claim: Our FMCG private label strategy follows the 20-20-20 principle delivering price advantage and margin.
claims.quote: And so therefore, wherever it makes sense for us, wherever we see that there is leverage that we can drive, we are participating and we are, driving that private label business.

claims.claim: We will double down on our investments on store additions because store financial metrics are not deteriorating online.
claims.quote: Considering what's happening in the country from a competitive context perspective, including QC, I think we will double down on our investments on store additions because we don't see our store financial metrics deteriorating because of online.

claims.claim: We pivoted from pickup and home delivery to a focused home delivery business.
claims.quote: While some of you may think that, that should have been the year for speed or accelerated expansion of e-Commerce, we looked at it in a different way because we pivoted from the pickup, plus home delivery to a more focused home delivery business because that is how the market evolved.

claims.claim: General merchandise and apparel gross margin contribution will stay around current run rate of 23%.
claims.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%, is the sense we get.

claims.claim: Quick commerce is not significantly impacting our metro revenues.
claims.quote: Surprisingly, it is not. If there is any one reason that impacts our metro revenues, it's actually our own ability to operate the store.

claims.claim: DMart Ready strategy is to consolidate, fix the model, and bring high throughputs in existing cities.
claims.quote: The strategy around the e-commerce business, the DMart Ready business is very consciously to be not very fast.

risks.text: Indirect tax matters of Rs 261.73 crores and income tax matters of Rs 3.82 crores.
Subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce Limited had continued losses with an investment carrying value of Rs 1,488.11 crore.
Inability to continue offering daily low prices could lead to loss of customers.
